- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.36) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (especially <0.2) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Forecast decay is too rapid after spikes — model overreacts to short-term sentiment surges, then drops too fast.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high in mid-to-late forecast horizon when sentiment weakens.
- Lagged sentiment influence: if sentiment drops after 3–5 days, model doesn’t adjust forecast downward quickly enough.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in first 5–7 days, then too low in last 10–15 days — model misjudges trend reversal timing.
- Spike correction: after a forecast spike >+5% from recent history, reduce next-day forecast by 2–3% to avoid overcorrection.
